components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Utility Button

components.css: .ds-btn-utility { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: var(--ink); background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--seam-strong); border-radius: 8px; padding: 9px 13px; font: 400 15px/1.5 var(--sans); cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms ease-out, border-color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-utility:hover { background: var(--surface-raised); border-color: var(--muted); } .ds-btn-utility:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-utility:active { background: var(--surface); }

components.name: Destructive Button

components.name: Text Field

components.css: .ds-runner { position: relative; padding: 22px 0 24px 20px; color: var(--ink); background: var(--ground); border-top: 1px solid var(--seam-strong); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--seam); font-family: var(--sans); } .ds-runner::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -24px; top: 31px; width: 28px; height: 1px; background: var(--seam-strong); } .ds-runner-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 18px; } .ds-runner-identity { min-width: 0; } .ds-runner-name { margin: 0; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: -0.02em; } .ds-runner-alias { margin-top: 3px; color: var(--signal); font: 12px/1.4 var(--mono); } .ds-runner-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 13px; } .ds-runner-lamp { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--faint); box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.35); } .ds-measurements { margin: 20px 0 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 14px 20px; } .ds-measure-label { color: var(--faint); font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-measure-value { margin: 4px 0 0; font: 13px/1.5 var(--mono); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-runner-foot { margin: 20px 0 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; } .ds-runner:hover { background: var(--topbar); } .ds-runner:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
The interface behaves like a persistent switching console: a severe but legible graphite field whose structure is exposed through hard seams, labelled channels, and an always-readable data hierarchy. The backplane is continuous rather than subdivided into a decorative card grid, so the operator reads the fleet as one connected system.

Operational truth is the only source of color or motion. Live state, warnings, failures, aliases, focus, and the restrained refresh pulse carry signal; everything else stays neutral. The result is dense enough for infrastructure work but calm enough to leave unknown values visibly unknown. Glass, gradients, ornamental imagery, and decorative effects are outside this visual language.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous dark backplane with hard structural seams.
Operational color only, assigned by state and action.
Space Grotesk for interface hierarchy; monospaced type for machine identity and telemetry.
Full-width runner channels instead of floating cards.
One restrained signal-rail pulse after a successful refresh.
Responsive reflow without horizontal scrolling or loss of the primary machine-connect action.

rules.name: The Operational Color Rule
rules.body: Color must report live state, interaction, or routing identity; it is never atmospheric decoration.

rules.name: The Fail-Closed Rule
rules.body: Offline state returns to neutral and preserves last-seen context; it never borrows the mint reserved for routable compute.

rules.name: The Data Voice Rule
rules.body: Human explanation uses Space Grotesk; machine identity, observation, and command output use the mono stack.

rules.name: The Honest Label Rule
rules.body: Unknown and unreported values receive the same typographic dignity as known values; never fade them into invisibility.

rules.name: The Backplane Continuity Rule
rules.body: Preserve the signal rail, connected channel marks, and full-width rows; do not break fleet state into independent cards.

rules.name: The Seam-over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with tonal planes and 1px structural seams; never lift an ordinary container into a card.

rules.name: The Hard Plane Rule
rules.body: Round controls for touch clarity, not containers for decoration; structural regions keep hard seams and square silhouettes.

rules.name: The In-Place State Rule
rules.body: Status lamps and plain-language availability copy change where they are; runner channels do not animate in from nowhere.

rules.name: The Primary Path Rule
rules.body: Keep machine enrollment visible as the main mint action, including the first mobile viewport, without giving routine or destructive actions equal emphasis.

dos: Do treat the runner fleet as one connected backplane with a signal rail and full-width channels.
Do reserve routable mint, attention amber, revocation coral, and relay cyan for their operational meanings.
Do use the locally bundled Space Grotesk for interface copy and the mono stack for machine-reported data.
Do preserve explicit `unknown`, `not reported`, and last-seen states.
Do keep **Connect machine** reachable in the first mobile viewport and keep measurement pairs free of horizontal scrolling.
Do honor reduced-motion preference by removing the refresh pulse.
donts: Don't turn fleet channels, metrics, or enrollment into a grid of floating cards.
Don't add gradients, glass, backdrop blur, decorative imagery, or ambient color.
Don't use shadows to separate ordinary regions; use graphite plane changes and 1px seams.
Don't use operational colors as decorative accents or interchange their meanings.
Don't hide uncertain telemetry, invent capability, or style missing data as though it were unimportant.
Don't let destructive actions share the filled mint silhouette of the primary path.
